acceptance.output_evidence:
THE READING, WITH NO VERDICT ON IT.

(a) MISLEADS TODAY, OR ONLY COULD? Today it mostly COULD. The three names have converged by accident -- built portal, superproject gitlink and served zip all read 5907cbca -- so a reader who resolves 'which portal' through the repo gets the right answer for the wrong reason, and nothing holds them together: the packer reads `git -C <portal> rev-parse HEAD` and never consults the gitlink (measured: the packer contains no ls-tree call). It DID mislead inside round 6: in the window 18:47:04Z -> 19:41:59Z the gitlink said 30ca034b while the served zip carried 18c0c5cb, and 30ca034b was not even an object in the portal clone, so a reader resolving through the gitlink then would have got a sha naming nothing. The live harm is not misdirection though -- it is INCOMPARABILITY. Two graph reads four hours apart in round 6 differ in their portal half and neither answer says so. W2-S63 armed exactly that; this census is its measurement: 5 served pushes, 2 with any portal record, 0 declared.

(b) WHICH OF FWD-3'S READERS WOULD NOTICE? The diff-taker would: the CTO's whole-graph node diff already prints a PROPS_KEY_DELTA across 27,665 nodes, and a portal-layer move would surface there as portal-layer adds/removes with nothing to attribute them to -- visible, but as noise. The reader who would NOT notice, and who is the actual exposure, is anyone who takes ONE read and cites its VINTAGE line: that line names the estate vintage and the stitch build and stops. Put in front of the L9 seat specifically: round 6's own stability argument (ROUND_ANALYSIS.round6.md s.3 -- 'the five magnitudes held UNCHANGED across three successive served vintages ... they held while things changed') spans a window in which the portal half moved from 18c0c5cb to 5907cbca. It does not overturn the sign -- the portal/src file count was 435 on both sides and the five magnitudes are measured quantities -- but 'things changed' did not know it included the portal commit, and a stability claim is stronger when it can name the variables it held constant and the ones it did not.

(c) WHOSE PLANE? Split, and the split is the point. The two DISPLAY hops (kuzu_nessie_load.read_stitch_vintage:71-77, projection_worker._age_line:257-262) are this project's engine and are genuinely cheap. The two FEED hops (packing a portal sha into the zip; stamping it into the marker in stitch-produce.tf) are not: they belong to whoever owns the portal extract route, and 0.7.0_AE_CloudOps already holds the disarm on W2-S40 and W2-S63. If the whole cell is treated as a globgrph display item, hops 3 and 4 will land, the served line will gain a clause, and the clause will render nothing -- a change that passes its own test and alters nothing a reader sees. That is the same failure mode as routing the remedy to format_provenance_header (W3-S17), arriving from the other direction. And underneath all of it sits an item that is not a vintage problem at all: hop 1 has no committed producer for the route that produced every served zip in round 6 -- five pushes, all by hand, all from a worker deliverable in a mission folder. Naming this cell 'the portal layer's vintage' and closing it with two display lines would leave that exactly where it is.
